fieldFixes.contribution: boyd spent a decade studying how teenagers use social media and argued, against the claim that young people do not care about privacy, that they work hard to achieve it within public networks — often by controlling who can understand a post rather than who can see it. In talks such as 'Networked Privacy' (2011) she argued that privacy is networked and collective: what relatives, friends and data-mining services reveal about us implicates us. She founded the Data & Society research institute and is now a professor of communication at Cornell.

fieldFixes.contribution: Nissenbaum proposed 'contextual integrity' (2004; expanded in her book Privacy in Context, Stanford University Press): privacy is violated when information flows break the norms of the context in which it was shared, rather than whenever something 'private' becomes known. With Daniel Howe at NYU she released TrackMeNot in 2006, a browser extension that hides a user's real searches in a stream of decoy queries. She later co-wrote Obfuscation: A User's Guide for Privacy and Protest (2015, with Finn Brunton) and directs the Digital Life Initiative at Cornell Tech.

fieldFixes.contribution: A co-author of the TLS security standard, Allen published 'The Path to Self-Sovereign Identity' in late April 2016 (his blog dates it 26 April), as the 22nd Internet Identity Workshop opened in Mountain View and ahead of the first ID2020 summit at the United Nations in May. Building explicitly on Kim Cameron's Laws of Identity, it set out ten principles — among them that users must control their identities, must consent to their use, and must disclose only the minimum. He also convened the #RebootingWebOfTrust design workshops on decentralised identity.
fieldFixes.influence: At the Internet Identity Workshop that week his ten principles were put on GitHub 'for comment and for further work', and they became a common reference point for self-sovereign identity; by 2018 Kaliya Young could tell a New America audience that 'a whole set of open standards around self-sovereign identity' had emerged.
